evidence.quote: According to the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) analyses with TEM, precipitated TCP phases in four alloys were all identified as µ phase, as reported previously [18].
TCP phases nucleated and grew up quickly from γ matrix in the original alloy sample (Fig 1(a)-(d)).
TCP precipitation is severely restrain ed by Ru addition as shown in Fig. 1(m)-(p), where few nucleus and precipitate was observed in p rimary γ matrix even after 45 minutes exposure (Fi.g. 1(p)).

the average sizes of TCP precipitates are decreased from over 200 nm in original alloy (Fig. 1(d)) to less 50 nm in alloy 3Ir (Fig. 1(l)).
Combining its large TCP size but s mall area fraction, it can be concluded that addition of element Ru can inhibit the nucleation of TCP phase efficiently.
Therefore, it is believed that the addition of Pt a nd Ir elements can slow down the growth rate of TCP phases, hence suppress the TCP precipitation in Fig. 3.
The role of Ru in suppressing TCP precipita tion is attributed to the so-called reverse partitioning effect.
